questions.q: What can global search typically look across in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: Both transactions (like invoices or journals) and setup/navigation items (like work areas or reports)
Only work area names
Only the current user's Favorites
Only data from the previous quarterly update
questions.explain: Global search can reach both transactional records and navigation/setup items, depending on configuration and the user's access.

options: A one-click shortcut to a specific page
Stored search or filter criteria on a specific list or search page, so a user doesn't re-enter the same filters every time
A record of every search a user has ever performed
A feature only available to administrators
questions.explain: A saved search stores filter criteria (such as 'invoices over $5,000, pending approval') so it can be re-run with one click instead of rebuilt each time.

questions.q: How does a Favorite differ from a saved search, according to this lesson?
options: There is no difference — they are the same feature
A Favorite can only be set by an administrator
A Favorite is a shortcut to a page, task, or report; a saved search is stored filter criteria on a list page
Saved searches can only be created during implementation, never afterward
questions.explain: A Favorite is a page-level shortcut, while a saved search stores a specific filter/criteria combination for a list or search page.

questions.q: In the example scenario of needing 'all invoices over $5,000, still pending approval, for the Manufacturing business unit' repeatedly, which tool is the best fit?
options: A Favorite
The Navigator
The springboard
A saved search
questions.explain: That scenario is a specific, reusable filter combination — exactly what a saved search is designed to store and re-run with one click.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say training end users on search, Favorites, and saved searches is valuable consulting work?
options: Because a user who only navigates through the full menu structure every time is working much harder than necessary
Because these tools are mandatory and cannot be skipped
Because Oracle disables the Navigator for untrained users
Because these tools replace the need for security roles
questions.explain: A proficient user combines global search, Favorites, and saved searches instead of relying solely on the full Navigator — teaching this meaningfully improves day-to-day efficiency.
